# E034 -- NASA Graphics Standards Manual

## Metadata
- **Company:** NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration)
- **Industry:** Government / Aerospace
- **Year:** 1976
- **Source file:** nasa_graphics_manual_nhb_1430-2_jan_1976-pdf.pdf
- **Pages:** 60
- **Language:** EN
- **Pages sampled:** 1-2, 6-7, 12-13

## Brand Strategy
- Titled "NASA Graphics Standards Manual" (NHB 1430.2), effective January 1, 1976
- Includes letter from Richard H. Truly (NASA Administrator)
- Purely a graphic standards manual -- no brand strategy, mission, or positioning content
- Functional purpose: standardize visual representation across the agency and all centers

## Logo
- NASA Logotype (the "worm") is the primary identity mark
- Agency Identification: logotype + full agency name ("National Aeronautics and Space Administration") in Helvetica Light, upper and lower case
- Center Identification: logotype + agency name + center name in Helvetica Medium (bold for primary emphasis)
- Reproduction art provided for every center: Headquarters, Ames, Goddard, Dryden, JPL, Johnson, Kennedy, Langley, Lewis, Marshall, Wallops, Stennis
- NASA Seal: reserved for award presentations, formal/ceremonial events only; never used alongside the logotype (visually incompatible)
- Mission Patches: occupy their own visual space, separated from official NASA identification; treated as unique elements with short duration
- Grid drawing provided for large-scale logotype applications
- Incorrect uses section included (page 1.6)

## Typography
- Sans Serif: Helvetica (agency name), Futura (publications)
- Serif: Garamond, Times Roman (publications)
- Dedicated typography pages in Section 5 (publications)
- Helvetica Light for agency name, Helvetica Medium for center names
- Typing Style specified for stationery (Section 3.3)

## Color
- "NASA Red" -- described as "a warm shade of red, a very active color which brings a kinetic dimension to the letterforms"
- Color described as reflecting "the lively and future-oriented character of NASA"
- Color swatches provided (Section 2.14)
- Dedicated color standards page (1.5) and color use page (1.4)

## Graphics
- Logotype is the core graphic element
- Grid drawing system for large applications
- Mission patches treated as separate graphic elements with their own visual space

## Photography
- Not covered in this manual

## Applications
- Section 3 -- Stationery: Letterheads, envelopes (HQ and centers), typing style, large envelopes, mailing labels, news releases
- Section 4 -- Forms
- Section 5 -- Publications
- Section 6+ -- likely additional applications (vehicles, signage, etc.) based on the comprehensive index

## Tone of Voice
- Not addressed -- purely a graphic standards manual
- However, the color description ("lively and future-oriented") reveals brand personality aspirations

## Outliers
- Historically iconic document -- the NASA "worm" logotype manual is one of the most celebrated identity systems in design history
- Scanned from physical document (Canon DR-7550C scanner) -- original 1976 print manual digitized in 2015
- Strict hierarchy between Logotype (daily use) and Seal (ceremonial only) -- they must never appear together
- Center-by-center reproduction art shows the scale of the identity system across a government agency
- The "worm" logotype was retired in 1992, brought back in 2020 -- this manual documents its original specifications

## Quality Score
- **Score: 4/5** -- A landmark identity manual that comprehensively covers logotype usage, color, typography, stationery, and applications across a complex multi-center organization. Historically significant as one of the foundational corporate identity manuals. Lacks brand strategy, tone of voice, and photography -- but these were not standard inclusions in 1976-era identity manuals. The systematic, modular structure is exemplary.
